name: The Ritz-Carlton, Santiago
positioning: Urban luxury hotel in the El Golf area of Las Condes, Santiago, with Chilean cuisine, a rooftop spa and an indoor pool
best_for: Travelers who want a polished city base in Las Condes
Food lovers drawn to New Chilean cuisine and pisco

facts.text: The hotel is at El Alcalde 15, in the El Golf area of Las Condes, Santiago.
Opened in 2003 as the first Ritz-Carlton in South America.
The Ritz-Carlton Bar has a dedicated pisco menu.
Café Ritual serves hand-roasted beans from Central and South America.
The spa is a rooftop sanctuary on the upper floors of the hotel.
The Club Level is on the 10th floor and is described as a hotel within a hotel.
Guest rooms have Diptyque bath amenities.
Gran Torre Santiago, the tallest building in South America, is a 15-minute walk away.
Beaches, skiing in the Andes and the Maipo Valley wine region are described as easily accessible from the hotel.
The Ritz-Kids program is for children aged 4 to 12.

highlights.text: New Chilean cuisine is the focus of Estró restaurant.
Spa guests can use an indoor pool under a glass cupola that opens onto an outdoor terrace overlooking Santiago.
Room design pays homage to Pre-Columbian craftsmanship with nature-inspired patterns and rich textures.
Estró's executive chef works with a local farm that grows half of its harvest for the hotel.

considerations.text: The hotel is 25.0 km from Arturo Merino Benitez International Airport.
Condé Nast Traveler says this is not really a kiddie kind of place.
WhataHotel notes the urban setting may lack resort-style recreational facilities.
